title: Emergence of a monopole phase in the $J_1{-}J_2$ Heisenberg model on the triangular lattice for small magnetic fields
authors: Sasank Budaraju, Shi Feng, Josef Willsher, Johannes Knolle, Frank Pollmann, Federico Becca
abstract: We investigate the ground-state phase diagram of the $J_1{-}J_2$ Heisenberg model on the triangular lattice under an external Zeeman field $H$ by using the variational Monte Carlo approach. We span a region with $0 \le J_2/J_1 \le 0.2$ and $0 \le H/J_1 \le 2$, to assess the fate of the (putative) spin-liquid phase that has been detected for $J_2/J_1=1/8$ at zero magnetic field. Simple variational ansatze are proposed for a few candidate states, and their energetics are compared on large clusters to obtain the phase diagram. For $J_2/J_1 \lesssim 1/6$, a continuous transition from a gapless "Y'' phase to a gapped "up-up-down'' phase is obtained, as predicted by spin-wave theory. Most importantly, around $J_2/J_1=1/8$, a condensate of monopoles (which are gapless gauge excitations of the spin liquid at $H=0$) is stabilized in a significant region of the phase diagram, for small Zeeman fields. Here, a finite scalar chirality is present, while no transverse magnetic order is detected. The stability of the monopole phase is confirmed by a field-theory approach that includes a self-consistent random-phase approximation of the low-lying spin fluctuations. The boundary between the monopole and "Y'' phases is also obtained with no free parameters.
summary: This work maps out the complex ground-state phase diagram of the $J_1{-}J_2$ Heisenberg model on a triangular lattice under an external magnetic field. Using Variational Monte Carlo, the authors identify a novel monopole phase stabilized near specific ratios of exchange couplings ($J_2/J_1=1/8$). This suggests that quantum fluctuations can stabilize topologically rich phases characterized by gauge excitations even when simple magnetic order is absent.
main_problem: The study investigates the ground-state phase diagram of the $J_1{-}J_2$ Heisenberg model on the triangular lattice when subjected to a small external Zeeman field ($H$).
main_result: The research finds that around $J_2/J_1=1/8$, a stable condensate of monopoles emerges in the phase diagram for small magnetic fields, characterized by finite scalar chirality but no transverse magnetic order.
method: Variational Monte Carlo (VMC) is employed to calculate variational energies across different candidate phases. This is supplemented by field-theory approaches and spin-wave theory analysis.
model_or_system: The system is the $J_1{-}J_2$ Heisenberg model on a triangular lattice, described by the Hamiltonian $H = J_1 \sum_{\langle i,jangle} \mathbf{S}_i \cdot \mathbf{S}_j + J_2 \sum_{\langle\langle i,kangleangle} \mathbf{S}_i \cdot \mathbf{S}_k - H \sum_i S_{z,i}$.
key_observables: Phase diagram dependence on $J_2/J_1$ and $H/J_1$; scalar chirality ($\chi$); magnetization curves; transverse structure factor.
important_parameters: $J_2/J_1 \le 0.2$ and $H/J_1 \le 2$. The critical point of interest is near $J_2/J_1=1/8$.
main_assumptions: The phase diagram construction relies on finite cluster calculations, which may underestimate the spin-liquid region at zero field compared to previous work.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the model's behavior in the parameter space, showing transitions between phases like 'Y', 'up-up-down', and the monopole phase. Specific plots show structure factors for different states vs. magnetization.
paper_structure: The paper systematically explores the ground state by comparing variational ansätze (e.g., Y, umbrella, monopole) using VMC to map out the phase diagram as a function of $J_2/J_1$ and $H/J_1$. Field-theory methods are used to confirm the stability of the emergent monopole phase.
why_interesting: The emergence of topologically non-trivial phases, such as monopole condensates, in frustrated quantum magnets is highly relevant for understanding exotic states beyond simple magnetic ordering, connecting strongly correlated physics to gauge theory concepts.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Phase diagram of the model (1) in the parameter range H/J1 ∈[0, 2] and J2/J1 ∈[0, 0.2], as estimated from VMC calcu- lations on the 18×18 triangular lattice. Vertical dashed lines indicate the values of J2/J1 for which VMC scans were performed (includ- ing the case with J2 = 0). At the phase boundaries, dashed (solid) lines denote continuous (first order) phase transitions. This figure is adapted from Ref. [29].

FIG. 2. Illustration of hopping parameters tij for the Y (a) and canted stripe (b) ans¨atze. Solid (dashed) lines denote positive (neg- ative) hopping amplitudes, and bonds in blue (black) denote ampli- tudes |tij| = ∆(|tij| = t). The flux through each triangular plaque- tte is 0 or π, following the Dirac spin liquid ansatz [6].

FIG. 3. (a) Energies (per site) of all the variational ans¨atze relative to that of the Y phase, on the 18 × 18 system. Errorbars are smaller than the size of the symbols. (b) Magnetization curve at J2 = 0, on the same cluster. A continuous transition from the Y phase to the UUD plateau is observed.

Top panels (a) - (c): Comparison of the energies ∆E(H) per site for the different ans¨atze relative to the state with the lowest energy at a given H, for J2/J1 = 0.1, J2/J1 = 0.125, and J2/J1 = 0.175.
